summary.text: Tom McClintock is the Republican incumbent in the 5th District, which stretches from the Sierra Nevada foothills to the Central Valley, and has served in the U.S. House since 2009.

He worked as a journalist and policy analyst before serving 22 years in the California Assembly and State Senate. In Congress he sits on the Judiciary, Natural Resources and Budget committees and chairs the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; his official biography highlights his record on federal spending and taxes.

paragraphs.text: McClintock was born in 1956 in Bronxville, New York, and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from UCLA in 1978.

He worked as a journalist and public policy analyst before holding office; according to Wikipedia, he was elected chair of the Ventura County Republican Party at age 23 and served as chief of staff to State Senator Ed Davis.

McClintock served in the California State Assembly from 1982 to 1992 and from 1996 to 2000, and in the California State Senate from 2000 to 2008; his official biography says he served 22 years in the state legislature.

He was twice the Republican nominee for State Controller, narrowly missing election in 2002 by 23/100ths of one percent, according to his official biography, and he ran as a candidate for governor in the 2003 recall election.

McClintock won election to the U.S. House on November 4, 2008, defeating Democrat Charlie Brown, and took office in 2009. His district now includes Yosemite National Park and, according to his official biography, stretches from Placerville to Modesto and on to Kings Canyon.

He is a member of the House Judiciary Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and sits on the Subcommittee on the Constitution and Limited Government.

He is a senior member of the House Natural Resources Committee; he chaired its Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries from 2011 to 2015 and its Subcommittee on Federal Lands from 2015 to 2018. He is also a member of the House Budget Committee.
His official biography says the National Taxpayers Union rated him the best vote for taxpayers in the House four times, most recently in 2020.
